user: Hi, I'm a freelance graphic designer and I opted for the 8% income tax rate.
response: As a freelancer who opted for the 8% income tax rate, your tax will be based on your gross sales or receipts, not on net income. Since you are under the 8% regime, you cannot deduct business expenses. Additionally, if your income comes purely from your freelance work, you may be entitled to a reduction of PHP 250,000 from your gross income before applying the 8% tax. However, if you have mixed income (from both freelance work and other sources), this reduction does not apply to your business income [S2, S3].

BIR Form 2307 is the Certificate of Creditable Tax Withheld at Source. It serves as proof that a certain amount of tax has been withheld from payments made to a taxpayer, typically for services rendered. This form is important for taxpayers as it can be used to claim tax credits against their income tax liability when filing their returns [S3].

response: No, as a mixed-income earner, you cannot subtract the ₱250,000 from your freelance income if you choose the 8% rate.
